Best Overall

Klein Tools 32500 11-in-1 Screwdriver / Nut Driver

4.8 ★ · 28,635 ratings

From $15.97 on Amazon — checked Nov 14, 2026. Prices move fast in Black Friday season, so confirm the live price.

11 tools in one handle8 bits: Phillips, slotted, Torx, square3 nut drivers: 1/4, 5/16, 3/8 in.Cushion-grip handleBits store in the shaft

The 32500 is built around one interchangeable shaft. Pull it out, flip it, swap the double-ended bits, and the same handle becomes a #1 or #2 Phillips, a slotted driver, a Torx, a square driver, or a 1/4, 5/16 or 3/8 in. nut driver — the sizes that turn up on hose clamps, appliance panels, furniture bolts and half the fixtures in a house. Nothing to charge, nothing to pair, and the bits live inside the shaft so there is no case to lose.

Why it tops this page: Klein is the brand electricians buy with their own money, and this is their most-gifted tool for a reason. The cushion grip is sized for real torque, the owner crowd is enormous and happy (4.8 stars, 28,635 ratings), and at under $20 it lands in the price band of a novelty gift while being the opposite of one. It also fits a stocking, a glovebox or the kitchen drawer where the house driver lives.

Honest trade-off It is not insulated — Klein sells a separate insulated version for live electrical work, and this one is not it. There is also no ratchet action, so long runs of screws are wrist work, and the double-ended bits are held in the shaft rather than a case: pull one out carefully over a floor drain.
The Verdict The one tool on this page we would hand to anyone — pro-grade, pocket-priced, used every week.

Buyer's Guide: How to Give Tools Under $25

Six rules that separate the gifts that get used from the gifts that get regifted.

01

Shop categories with nothing expensive inside

Under $25 fails in power tools, where a battery platform eats the whole budget, and succeeds in hand tools, lights, gloves, bags and gauges — categories with no motor to pay for. That is how a $16 Klein is a pro tool while a $16 drill is a toy. Pick the category first and the budget stops being a handicap.

02

Read the rating AND the crowd

A 4.8 from 28,635 owners (the Klein) is evidence. A 5.0 from twelve owners is a hope. On this page the smallest crowd is 4,825 ratings, and the biggest is 73,048 — every pick has been bought, used and judged at scale before it was recommended here.

03

Wear items are the safest gifts

The hardest person to buy for already owns the obvious tools. He does not own fresh gloves — his are worn through. He does not own a spare headlamp — his was borrowed in March. Gloves, lights and glovebox tools wear out, wander off and live in second locations, which makes them the gifts that never duplicate.

04

One great tool beats forty-piece filler

Gift sets compete on piece counts: 40, 80, 120 pieces of soft metal and good intentions. Pros compete on one tool done right. A single 11-in-1 from the brand electricians carry will outlive a novelty set by a decade — and the receiver can tell the difference the first time he uses it.

05

Check the price the week you buy

Every price on this page was verified on November 14, 2026 — and November is the most volatile pricing month of the year. Amazon’s Black Friday deals start November 19, and under-$25 staples are exactly what gets discounted. A pick that is $23.39 today may be $18 next week, or sell through and jump. The budget rule is simple: check the live price, and if it has drifted over $25, another pick on this page will not have.

06

Mind the variant traps

Small tools hide their differences in the options row. Gloves price by size and color (our Mechanix link is Large/Blue for a reason). Headlamps come in battery and rechargeable versions that look identical — ours is the USB rechargeable 2-pack. Drivers come in bit counts that change the tool. Use the links on this page and you land on the exact variant we checked.

Frequently Asked Questions

What is the best tool gift under $25?

For most people, the Klein Tools 32500 11-in-1 screwdriver. It is a genuine pro tool — the multi-driver electricians carry — with eight bits and three nut driver sizes in one cushion-grip handle, it costs under $20, and it gets used on real jobs every week. The other picks win on specific needs: the Lepro headlamp 2-pack for anyone who works in dark corners, Mechanix gloves for hands that take a beating, the WORKPRO bag for a DIYer whose tools live in a drawer, and the AstroAI gauge as a glovebox stocking stuffer.

Are these gifts really all under $25?

Yes — every price on this page was read from the product's Amazon listing on November 14, 2026: the Klein from $15.97, the Lepro 2-pack from $18.99, the Mechanix gloves at $23.39 in Large/Blue, the WORKPRO bag from $14.07 and the AstroAI gauge from $12.79. Two honest caveats: glove prices vary a little by size and color, and Amazon prices move quickly in Black Friday season, in both directions. Check the live price before you buy — if one has drifted over $25, the others still hold the budget.

What do you buy a man who already has every tool?

Buy the things that wear out, wander off, or live somewhere new. Gloves wear out — a fresh pair of Mechanix is always used. Headlamps get borrowed and lost — a rechargeable 2-pack replaces the one that vanished. And a digital tire gauge belongs in the glovebox, not the toolbox, so it is never a duplicate of what's on his bench. The picks on this page were chosen with exactly that problem in mind.

Is the Klein 32500 a real tool or a stocking-stuffer gimmick?

A real tool. The 32500 is the standard multi-bit driver in a lot of electricians' pouches: eight industrial bits (Phillips, slotted, Torx and square) plus 1/4, 5/16 and 3/8 in. nut drivers, all carried in one interchangeable shaft. Its 4.8 stars come from 28,635 ratings, most of them from people who use it for work. One limit to know: it is not insulated, so it is not the driver for live electrical work.

Which of these actually fit in a stocking?

The AstroAI gauge and the Klein driver are true stocking size. The Lepro headlamps come in a small box that fits a stocking top or a gift bag. The Mechanix gloves roll up small enough for a stocking, too. The WORKPRO bag is the under-the-tree gift of the five — it is a 12-inch bag, and it arrives empty, ready to be filled with the other four.

Why do the prices here say 'from'?

Because most of these products have more than one seller or variant, and the number we print is the lowest live offer for the exact product when we checked on November 14, 2026. 'From $15.97' means the Klein started at $15.97 that day — your size, color or seller may price a little differently. We would rather show a real, dated starting price than a round number that was never true.

The Bottom Line

If you buy one gift, buy the Klein 32500 — it is the rare under-$20 tool with nothing toy about it. For the man who works in dark places, the Lepro headlamp 2-pack is two gifts in one box; for hands that take a beating, fresh Mechanix gloves are always spent well. The WORKPRO bag organizes the DIYer whose tools live in a drawer, and the AstroAI gauge is the $13 stocking stuffer every driver needs. All five were under $25 when checked — confirm the live price, and you cannot go far wrong.
